questions.question: Which programming language should the mobile app use? Python was explicitly requested; the listed language choices are limited to TypeScript and JavaScript, so review the framework choice for how Python will be handled.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use TypeScript for a cross-platform mobile application.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use JavaScript for a cross-platform mobile application.

questions.rationale: The user explicitly requests Python. The language selector is restricted to TypeScript or JavaScript; this recommendation is not confirmation to replace Python. The framework answer must retain the Python request and its platform constraints for explicit review.

questions.question: How should the app handle the requested Python implementation across Android, Huawei HarmonyOS, and Apple iOS? Review Python framework feasibility and platform limitations; do not treat Android-APK compatibility as native HarmonyOS support.
questions.recommendedChoice: Python with Kivy, subject to packaging and device validation; Android is the most practical target, iOS packaging is possible but has additional Xcode/build and distribution constraints, and HarmonyOS support is limited to devices with Android-APK compatibility. No claim of HarmonyOS NEXT native support.

options.label: Python with Kivy, subject to packaging and device validation; Android is the most practical target, iOS packaging is possible but has additional Xcode/build and distribution constraints, and HarmonyOS support is limited to devices with Android-APK compatibility. No claim of HarmonyOS NEXT native support.
options.description: Keep Python as the requested implementation language. Kivy is a practical Python-first candidate for Android and has an iOS packaging path, but build, store-distribution, and device compatibility need validation. Huawei HarmonyOS may run an Android APK on compatible devices; this is not native HarmonyOS or HarmonyOS NEXT support.

questions.rationale: Python can be retained as a Python-first mobile approach, with Kivy as a candidate, but it does not provide equivalent native support across all three ecosystems. Confirm target expectations before planning; a TypeScript/native or Flutter alternative must not be substituted without explicit approval.

questions.question: Which fitness-record features and operating mode are required?
questions.recommendedChoice: Customize workout plans; choose trained body parts; log exercises with reps, sets, and weight; record sessions; view training-load trends, monthly training count, and body parts trained; record body weight and view body-weight/body-change trends. Prefer private on-device records unless cloud sync is explicitly requested.
questions.answer: Customize workout plans; choose trained body parts; log exercises with reps, sets, and weight; record sessions; view training-load trends, monthly training count, and body parts trained; record body weight and view body-weight/body-change trends. Cloud sync and accounts were not requested.
questions.rationale: The feature list is taken directly from the user. Local-only storage is a conservative default; cloud sync should not be assumed.

questions.question: Which data stores should the app use?

options.label: No datastore required

questions.rationale: The request does not call for a backend or cloud sync. Device-local persistence is part of the mobile app, not a provisioned Azure datastore.
